CSO Planner Board Scheduling Progress Metric on Grouped Equipment Lines

A scheduling progress metric is being introduced on grouped Equipment lines in the CSO Planner Board. The metric is displayed as a badge on the grouped Equipment cell and reflects how much of the planned labour has been scheduled for the selected period.

The calculation compares the total duration of trips scheduled during the selected period with the total labour class hours defined for those services, aggregated across all equipment in the group.

On hover, the badge displays a breakdown showing scheduled hours against total planned hours.

Visibility of the metric can be controlled via Planner Board user settings or System Setup.

System.Description.newValue:
As a planner, I would like to know how many hours of my estimated work have actually been scheduled. So initially, I will be planning the CSOs by estimating how many hours each labour class will need, and then I will be scheduling actual technicians to the service orders and would like to have an overview of how much scheduling is still left to do for the equipment.

For example, the equipment record has the following CSOs listed with the estimated labour classes:
  • CSO 1
    • Senior Engineer 2 hours
    • Junior Engineer 4 hours
  • CSO 2
    • Senior Engineer 3 hours
    • Junior Engineer 4 hours
    • Mechanic 5 hours
  • CSO 3
    • Senior Engineer 1 hour
    • Junior Engineer 2 hours
    • Electrician 3 hours
    • Apprentice 4 hours

And CSO 1 and 2 have actual trips already scheduled:
  • CSO 1
    • trip 1: 3 hours
    • trip 2: 2 hours
  • CSO 2
    • trip 2 hours
Then on the grouped Equipment line, I would like to see 7/28 (7 hours are scheduled out of 28 estimated).

For more context: EPSA has the concept of Estimated, Planned and Actual hours. The estimated hours are the high-level planning, broken down by labour class; planned hours are the hours on the trips; and actual hours are the actual time spent completing the trips.

Custom.ResolutionNotes.newValue:
What was changed
When the CSO Planner Board is grouped by Equipment, each equipment's grouped row now shows a chip with the hours of trips scheduled against that equipment's total estimated labour-class hours (e.g. 7/28 HRS), with a hover tooltip spelling the same figures out in words.
A new Planner Board Suitelet endpoint aggregates both figures server-side for the CSOs currently listed under each equipment.

AC coverage
AC 1 badge on the Equipment grouped line showing X/Y
New EquipmentSchedulingProgressBadgeComponent (equipment-scheduling-progress-badge.component.ts|html|scss), injected into the equipment row via [subtitleTemplate]="badgeTemplate" on equipment-parent-card.component.html.
Only appears when grouped by Equipment: the effect filters on selectedGrouping?.scriptId === NS_SERVICE_ORDER_FIELD_ID.EQUIPMENT, and the template guard is isServiceOrderPlannerGroupedByEquipment() && resource.isParent. Grouping by Customer, Service Zone or anything else keeps the plain resource card.
Values are rounded to whole hours (DecimalPipe '1.0-0'). See drift note 2 on the HRS suffix.
AC 1a X = hours of trips scheduled across the CSOs shown under the equipment
getEquipmentSchedulingProgress pbTrip.getServiceOrderScheduledHoursMap({ serviceOrderIds }) in cmms_pb_trip_module.js.
Sums custrecord_cmms_techtimealloc_hours on customrecord_cmms_tech_time_allocation (published) plus custrecord_cmms_prov_trip_duration on customrecord_cmms_prov_technician_trip (draft), filtered to isinactive = false.
Drafts are restricted to genuinely unpublished ones custrecord_cmms_prov_trip_prov_cso = @NONE@ and custrecord_cmms_prov_trip_tech_trip = @NONE@ so a draft that's already been promoted isn't double counted.
Crew trips count once per crew trip, not once per crew member. A crew trip is stored as one technician-trip record per member, each carrying the whole duration, so getScheduledHoursMapByTripSearch dedupes on custrecord_cmms_techtimealloc_crw_trp_id / custrecord_cmms_prov_trip_crew_offlineid. Without it X doubled (1 scheduled hour showed as 2).
Scope is the CSO ids currently loaded under that equipment: the effect walks resource.children and excludes the SKELETON_ID_PREFIX, NO_GROUPING_CHILDREN_PREFIX and SHOW_MORE_PREFIX placeholders.
AC 1b Y = labour class hours across those CSOs
pbCommon.getServiceOrderLaborClassHoursMap({ serviceOrderIds, serviceSetupIds, serviceOrderServiceSetupMap }), summed as (duration numberOfTechnicians).
The multiplier is required it's the app's existing definition, the same one behind the labour-class-hours chips on CSO cards. Summing duration alone reported 10 instead of 20 on a two-technician labour class.
Service make/model per CSO resolved by getServiceOrderServiceSetupMapByServiceOrderIds reading customrecord_cmms_equipment_service.custrecord_cmms_eqsrv_service_makemodel.
AC 2 hover tooltip
New i18n key EQUIPMENT-SCHEDULING-PROGRESS.TOOLTIP; en = "{{ scheduledHours }} hours are scheduled out of {{ laborClassHours }} labour class hours." the AC sentence verbatim.
Opens on mouseenter of the chip, closes 200 ms after mouseleave; the close is cancelled if the pointer moves onto the tooltip so it doesn't vanish in transit. Anchored to the chip via a generated tooltipAnchorId.
Styled to the design via .equipment-progress-tooltip in styles.scss (#353535 background, 12px white text, 5px radius, shadow 0 0 6px rgba(53,53,53,.2)). It lives in the global stylesheet because Angular view encapsulation can't reach Mobiscroll's popup elements.
AC 3 board date range does not affect the totals
Honoured. Neither X nor Y is date filtered: getEquipmentSchedulingProgress accepts only serviceOrderIds, the trip search carries no date clause, and the effect no longer reads dateRangeSelector.
AC 4 no badge when Y = 0
isVisible = computed(() => totalLaborClassHoursValue() > 0), with the chip wrapped in @if (isVisible()).
Covers the other zero paths too: an equipment with no CSOs dispatches 0/0; a failed request leaves the values null (reset when the action is dispatched, no failure reducer) which ?? 0 treats as zero so the badge hides rather than showing stale numbers.
QA behaviour note: the badge hides and re-appears on each page load / resource reload, since the reducer resets both values to null on dispatch.
Supporting change grouped row sizing (not in the AC)
The taller equipment card was being clipped: Mobiscroll sizes grouping rows from a hidden empty probe and writes the result as an inline min-height that the stylesheet couldn't override. Added GroupingRowHeightService (publishes the tallest reported height), a ResizeObserver in ResourceCardComponent that measures the resource cell not the card, which sits inside a padded .mbsc-timeline-resource-title and under-reported by 14px and SchedulerComponent publishing .service-order-grouping-rows + --service-order-grouping-row-height on mbsc-eventcalendar. styles.scss then applies min-height: var(--service-order-grouping-row-height, 3.25em) !important to .mbsc-timeline-parent and 18.75em to the resource column, scoped under .cso-scheduler so it can't leak into the calendar or delivery planners, which share that ancestor class.

AC drift
Badge position AC says "next to the Equipment name"; implemented in the resource card's subtitle slot, i.e. directly below the name. Follows the attached design screenshot.
Format AC says "two numbers in the format X/Y"; the badge renders X/Y HRS. The suffix and integer rounding come from the design, not the AC.
Date filter cycled in and out. Commit f0e3eae64 added a date filter to X; c8f8f8d reverted it after PM confirmed the AC wording stands. Net result is AC-compliant flagging it because a reviewer scanning the history will see "add date filter" and may assume the totals are date filtered.
Scope reading. X and Y cover the CSOs currently loaded under the equipment. If an equipment has more than one page, the "Show more" row is excluded, so only the loaded page contributes. We read AC's "shown under the Equipment" as the currently displayed set.
Translations beyond the AC. The English sentence is the AC's; the same key was added to the other 19 locales. The non-English strings were machine-authored in this story and need native review before release. Several existing LABOR-CLASS-HOURS strings in the repo mistranslate "labour class" as a social class (fr-FR "classe ouvrire", it-IT "classe operaia", nl-NL "Arbeidersklasse", fi-FI "Tyvenluokan"); I deliberately did not copy those patterns.
Row-sizing work is additional to the AC and is required for the design to render correctly.
